newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Greenpeace says Brazil imports banned batteries.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace says Brazil imports banned batteries.

text.p: Brazil continues to import used car batteries from the United States, despite banning the trade amid fears of health risks last year, environmental group Greenpeace said on Monday.
Brazilian battery manufacturer Grupo Moura imported about 5,000 tonnes of lead batteries for recycling from the United States in the first six months of 1997, Greenpeace said in a report.
"If Brazil and the United States care about protecting public health and the environment, this trade should stop immediately," said Marcelo Furtado of Greenpeace International in Washington.

Last year, Greenpeace said it detected lead contamination levels in soil near a Moura recycling facility which were four times above the amount considered dangerous by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.
That report contributed to a decision by the Brazilian government to prohibit used car battery imports.

A Grupo Moura official confirmed the company was importing used car batteries but said its purchases had been authorised by customs. "We did nothing illegal. We have all the necesssary paperwork," Moura's commercial director Luiz Mello said.

But an official at Brazil's Environment Ministry insisted that imports of used car batteries were prohibited. "There is no doubt about it, the importation of these items is not allowed," said the official.

The United States is the only member of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) which has not joined an international agreement to phase out the trade in hazardous waste between rich and poor countries, Greenpeace said.
